text:
maria: heads up — after the kernel-6.3 rollout to eu-west2 GPU pool (p4s) we’re seeing repeated PCIe link retrain/disconnects and NCCL allreduce times spiking 4-6x. some jobs hit Xid 31 + occasional driver oops.

aj: can you paste dmesg snippet? we rolled this through the usual canary yesterday.

maria: sure — grabbing the latest from node p4-eu-021.

```
[ 1234.567890] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Multiple Corrected error received: id=0000
[ 1234.567895] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: PCIe Bus Error: severity=Corrected, type=Physical Layer, id=0010(Receiver ID)
[ 1240.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID=8745, GPU=0: Xid is 31: a system memory read trap
[ 1240.123460] mlx5_core 0000:af:00.0: mlx5e nic reset: link down
[ 1240.123465] nv-peer-mem: unload
```

ryan: interesting — both GPU errors and mlx5 NIC resets. sounds like something in 6.3 changed PCIe link training or DMA ordering.

sasha: i’m seeing the same symptoms on a few p4 nodes in us-west1 where we applied the same kernel, but less frequent. maybe region rollout timing difference.

aj: do we have any NCCL logs? if RDMA goes flaky, NCCL falls back to TCP and perf tanks.

maria: attaching a trimmed NCCL debug from a 64-GPU allreduce that slowed from ~120ms -> ~600ms.

```
[2026-03-17 14:02:03] NCCL INFO comm 0x7f8ddc0: Using transport: ib
[2026-03-17 14:02:05] NCCL WARN AllReduce rank 12: peer 5: ib timeout, falling back
[2026-03-17 14:02:05] NCCL INFO fallback to socket transport
[2026-03-17 14:02:07] NCCL INFO AllReduce time: 612ms
```

deepa: confirmed — RDMA/ib reports link flaps around the same time. i think mlx5 firmware + kernel 6.3 net stack change is the culprit.

ops-bot: Deploy bot: kernel-6.3 rollout initiated for eu-west2 gpu-pool at 2026-03-17T13:55:00Z.

aj: immediate mitigation: cordon and drain affected nodes, roll back kernel package or boot into previous kernel, and fail jobs to spare capacity. we should also pause further kernel rollouts until root cause.

maria: started cordoning p4-eu-020..p4-eu-025. evicting long-running jobs now.

ryan: how many nodes affected total? need capacity plan for customer impact.

maria: ~12 p4 nodes showing PCIe AER events, ~40% of eu-west2 GPU pool degraded. estimated job slowdown is causing ~2x slot-hours increase for queued work.

deepa: that's a material cost spike — queued batch jobs are retrying and staying longer. should we spin up on-demand in other regions (us-west1) while we triage? that has cross-region data transfer implications.

aj: yes spin up temporary capacity in us-west1 and gc region-wide autoscaler to cover SLA. we need to notify SRE and sales about potential customer impact.

ci-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-033 — kernel-6.3 gpu node regressions (eu-west2). Priority: High.

sasha: quick trouble-shoot idea — can someone try booting a failing node into 5.15 kernel and run a short NCCL allreduce? if perf recovers that's strong evidence.

maria: doing that now on p4-eu-021 — will report back in ~10m.

(10 minutes)

maria: booted p4-eu-021 on 5.15-rt. reran same allreduce, time back to ~130ms, no mlx5 resets in dmesg. seems likely kernel 6.3 regression with PCIe/ib interaction.

aj: OK we stop the rolling upgrade and prepare a rollback strategy for eu-west2. action items:
- aj: coordinate rollback plan + hold on further kernel upgrades (assigned)
- maria: finish cordoning/evicting remaining bad nodes + start repro logs (assigned)
- deepa: provision cross-region temporary capacity and estimate cost delta (assigned)
- sasha/ryan: prepare customer comms and internal incident timeline (assigned)

ryan: ETA for rollback?

aj: if package available, we can stage rollback tonight and execute early-morning maintenance window to avoid peak jobs. need approvals from oncall.

deepa: cost rough calc — moving 40% of eu-west2 GPU workload to us-west1 at current spot rates + transfer means ~+18% monthly run cost if issue persists for a week. flagging finance.

maria: also captured full nv/ib stack traces and a kernel + mlx5 firmware diff to attach to upstream bug. will open an issue with vendor and cc the kernel folks.

sasha: thanks. keep the thread updated. :thumbsup:
